SignalsLink.YTT
Connects the Freight Dock and Chunk Anchor to trains from Yang's Transport Tycoon. It allows the Freight Dock to load and unload a train that stops at it, and allows the anchor to wake up when a train approaches it.

Loading and unloading trains
Write a header containing the word train on the Freight Dock's paper. The header must be on its own line and separated from the rules below it by a blank line:
• unload train — from the train into the Freight Dock's crate
• load train — from the Freight Dock's crate into the train
• from train to yard — directly from the train to the storage yard
• from yard to train — directly from the storage yard into the train
Write rules below the header just as for other devices; see Paper conditions. How headers work in general is described under Freight Dock.
The Freight Dock waits for the train to stop. Every car it works with must be stationary. It searches for trains within 12 blocks of the Freight Dock, and if more cars are in range, it starts with the nearest one.
The word train itself means the cargo space of all cars in range: boxcars, refrigerator cars, and minecarts.

Example paper with two sections:
unload train boxcar

game:ingot-*

load train engine

game:charcoal
keep 16
The first section unloads all ingots from boxcars into the crate. The second fills the firebox with charcoal and keeps 16 pieces there.

Qualifiers after the word train
After the word train, you can specify which train and which part of it the section applies to. Words can be combined, and their order does not matter.
• north, south, east, west — only the train on that side of the Freight Dock. n, s, e, w are also sufficient.
• north5 — only the train standing exactly five blocks north of the Freight Dock. Useful where several tracks run next to each other. The number can be 1 to 12.
• 2 — only the second vehicle in the train. Counted from the front of the train, which is number 1.
• boxcar — only boxcars.
• fridge — only refrigerator cars, specifically their cargo space.
• cart — only minecarts with a crate.
• fridge 2 — the second refrigerator car from the front. With a car type, the number is counted only among cars of that type, so it still works if you rearrange the train.
• engine — fuel and water of the steam engine, both in a locomotive and a steam car. Without this word, nothing is loaded into the firebox.
• ice — the refrigerator car's cooling slots, meaning the space for ice. Without this word, ice goes into the cargo space like any other goods.
Words that do not make sense together, such as boxcar ice or engine fridge, are reported by the paper as an error.

Header examples:
unload train north — unloads the train standing to the north
load train boxcar — loads only into boxcars
load train fridge 2 south — into the second refrigerator car of the train to the south
load train engine — replenishes fuel and water
load train ice — replenishes ice in refrigerator cars
from train cart to yard north — directly from minecarts to the yard to the north

Chunk Anchor
The anchor's dialog gains a Wake when a train approaches toggle. A sleeping anchor then wakes up as soon as a train is heading to its station, even if it is traveling outside players' view, and does not sleep until the train arrives. The chunks are therefore loaded before the train arrives, allowing it to appear at the station and be unloaded.
As long as a train is standing in the anchor's area, the anchor also keeps the columns beneath its cars loaded and does not sleep. These columns are charged like any other.
The column selection must cover the entire stationary train, not just the station building. A train that does not fit within the kept columns only passes through the station and unloads nothing.
Without this mod, anchors on a server with Yang's Transport Tycoon disable themselves and tell you why.

For server administrators
On startup, the mod checks whether it understands the installed version of Yang's Transport Tycoon. If not, it disables train loading and writes this to the server log. Other parts of SignalsLink continue to run.
The AnchorApproachBlocks option in the signalslink.json file determines how far before the station the anchor wakes up. The default value is 160 blocks.
